notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix (none found; kb/Work PB5086, landed, names "RERUN's null facility against §1985:VII.2.12.4 GR2" as a sibling still owed, and PB4945, landed, covered the five syntax rules only). §1985:VII.2.12.4 GR1: "The RERUN clause specifies when and where the rerun information is recorded", in two ways: "a. If file-name-1 is specified, the rerun information is written on each reel or unit of an output file" at a place the implementor specifies, and "b. If implementor-name is specified, the rerun information is written as a separate file on a device specified by the implementor." Implemented at 85: the source side. rerunClause and rerunEvery parse the clause, VisitRerunClause is the edition arm (accepted at --std 85, COBOL0902 from 2002), and ScreenRerunClauses, called by BindIoControl, makes GR1's distinction between the two ways (the ON word is file-name-1 when it names a file of the program and implementor-name-1 otherwise) and asks the clause's syntax rules of each. Not implemented: either way of recording. BindIoControl keeps nothing of a RERUN clause after the screen (its summary: "a null rerun facility is conforming"), no member of CodeGen or the runtime reads the clause, and a probe with both ways (ON a file with END OF REEL, ON an implementor-name with 1 RECORDS) writes no rerun information: the file named in ON is never created and no separate file appears. The RERUN clause is not in the Hardware Dependent Language Element List (§1985:p.XVII-94 lists the MULTIPLE FILE TAPE clause, not RERUN), so §1985:I.1.5.2.2 applies ("An implementation must accept the syntax and provide the function for all Standard COBOL language elements"), and §1985:I.1.5.2.3 requires support of obsolete elements. docs/CONFORMANCE.md has no line for the clause; the null-facility posture is docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md row 7.15's and no owner decision records it. Same absence as the row 1985-GR-VII.2.12.4-2 (the seven forms). The witness writes RERUN ON a file EVERY END OF REEL OF an output file and checks only that the program runs.

next.reason: 1985: "The RERUN clause specifies when and where the rerun information is recorded."; 2023: "No 2023 clause holds the RERUN clause; no candidate covers rerun information or its recording.". No 2023 clause carries the RERUN clause. The wording candidates cover DELETE, READ, OPEN, CLOSE and similar statements, none of them rerun information, so the clause is dropped.
